tja.explanation: "Tja" means "well". Use it when you are unsure and still thinking: "Kommer du?" "Tja, måske." (Are you coming? Well, maybe.)

to.explanation: "To" means "two". To count things, put it before the noun: "to børn" (two children), "to æg" (two eggs). In numbers like 22 the ones come first: "toogtyve" (twenty-two) is literally "two-and-twenty".

to gange.explanation: "To gange" means "twice". Literally, it is "two times". To say how often something happens, add "om dagen" (a day), "om ugen" (a week) or "om måneden" (a month): "to gange om ugen" (twice a week).

tofu.explanation: "Tofu" means "tofu". To name an amount, say "en pakke tofu" (a package of tofu).

toiletpapir.explanation: "Toiletpapir" means "toilet paper". It is built from "et toilet" (a toilet) and "papir" (paper). To name an amount, say "en rulle toiletpapir" (a roll of toilet paper).

told.explanation: "Told" means "customs". It also means a tax on goods from abroad, which English calls "duty": "Man skal betale told" (You have to pay duty).

tolerant.explanation: "Tolerant" means "tolerant", spelled the same as in English. To say the opposite, add "in-": "en intolerant person" (an intolerant person).

tolv.explanation: "Tolv" means "twelve". To say a dozen, use "et dusin": "et dusin æg" (a dozen eggs).

tolvte.explanation: "Tolvte" means "twelfth". To say a date, use "den tolvte december" (the twelfth of December).

tom.explanation: "Tom" means "empty". To say the opposite, use "fuld" (full): "en fuld flaske" (a full bottle). The word "fuld" also means "drunk" for a person: "Han er fuld" (He is drunk).

tomhændet.explanation: "Tomhændet" means "empty-handed". It is built from "tom" (empty) and "en hånd" (a hand).

torden.explanation: "Torden" means "thunder". It is the noun for "at tordne" (to thunder). To say it is thundering right now, say "Det tordner" (It is thundering).

torsdag.explanation: "Torsdag" means "Thursday". In Danish, day names are not capitalized, unlike English "Thursday". To say "on Thursday" for the coming one, use "på torsdag": "Vi ses på torsdag" (See you on Thursday). To say "on Thursdays", use "om torsdagen": "Jeg træner om torsdagen" (I work out on Thursdays). Do not mix it up with "tirsdag" (Tuesday): "Vi ses torsdag" (See you Thursday), "Vi ses tirsdag" (See you Tuesday).

torsk.explanation: "Torsk" means "cod". To talk about the animal, say "en torsk" (a cod). To talk about the food, use "torsk" alone: "Vi spiser torsk" (We eat cod).

tortur.explanation: "En tortur" means "torture". It also describes something very unpleasant: "Det var en tortur at vente" (Waiting was torture).

tosproget.explanation: "Tosproget" means "bilingual". It is built from "to" (two) and "et sprog" (a language). It also describes things in two languages: "et tosproget skilt" (a bilingual sign).

tosset.explanation: "Tosset" means "silly". A silly person is called "en tosse" (a silly person).

total.explanation: "Total" means "total". To make another word stronger, use "totalt" (totally) before it: "Jeg er totalt træt" (I am totally tired).

totalt.explanation: "Totalt" means "totally". It is built from "total" (total) and the ending "-t". To make an adjective stronger, put it before: "Han er totalt ligeglad" (He does not care at all).

traditionel.explanation: "Traditionel" means "traditional". To say traditional food, use "traditionel mad" (traditional food). To say the opposite, use "moderne" (modern): "et moderne hus" (a modern house).

trafik.explanation: "Trafik" means "traffic". To say a traffic jam, use "en trafikprop" (literally, a traffic plug): "Der er en trafikprop på broen" (There is a traffic jam on the bridge).

tragisk.explanation: "Tragisk" means "tragic". The noun is "en tragedie" (a tragedy): "Branden var en tragedie" (The fire was a tragedy).

trang.explanation: "Trang" means "cramped". To say a room has too little space, use it before the noun: "et trangt rum" (a cramped room). For clothes it means "tight": "trange bukser" (tight pants). To talk about little money, use "trange kår" (hard circumstances): "at leve på trange kår" (to live on very little).

travl.explanation: "Travl" means "busy". To say you are in a hurry, use "at have det travlt" (to be in a hurry): "Jeg har det travlt" (I am in a hurry).

tre.explanation: "Tre" means "three". To count things, put it before the noun: "tre børn" (three children), "tre æg" (three eggs).
